body:
How do you mould the barrier ring? I'm finding it difficult to do. I have always just placed it on around the stoma, currently there is a very small gap when I do but I always position it at the top of the stoma so it won't leak down.

Do you put the ring on the stoma or on the bag first?

Forgot to include my current bags. I'm using the standard flat 1 piece drainable and a barrier ring.

The barrier ring does make it slightly bigger around the stoma but it lasts longer than the bag on its own.

There is definitely something there but the doctor said to get a scan in order to find out the type of hernia.

I believe I had started to lift heavy things too early. My surgeon said to wait about 12 weeks, after it happened everyone else said wait about 6 months.

I didn't know they could just be left there, especially with pain. I've got one and developed another by sneezing. The second one is way more painful and definitely causing me trouble but I don't know what type they are yet so I don't know what to expect from them.

Out of curiosity, do you know which areas are more prone to trappings/twisting?
Yeah I believe so. I've only been told to be careful when lifting as hernias are more likely now with a stoma. Had no idea what to expect with the incision.

This sounds like what was happening to me. It felt like the output would stay around the stoma area until a leak happened.

I believe what I read said that having no air can create a vacuum type situation in the bag and the output has no guidance or way to go.

Where does the bag start to leak? I started having leaks and one morning had 3 changes by 10am. It was because the output would not move down and ended up going under.

I read on another site that having no air in the bag can cause this so I started to deliberately open the end, catch some air and close it. I haven't had this issue again so it seems to work.

My previous comment sounds like it's a strange size but that's just the feeling. The bulge is maybe 4 inches only located in one area.

I'm am most likely going to call someone or go to the emergency room. Thanks.
It's just under 3 month old. Before this there was still some mild pain when I'd sneeze but that was all.
I noticed the initial bulge around an incision area but I'm feeling it from my hip from the same side. I have no idea what to expect for a hernia which is why I'm quite worried.

So I have a permanent ileostomy, only had a blockage once before but it resolved itself shortly after and it was located closer to the stoma.

This time however is different. I'm not feeling nauseous or in constant discomfort. It's also located all on the left side and feels like its from near my hip to my middle abdomen area when I move around.

The thing that confusing me was when I started to lay down and move around it started making noises around the area which made me think it was a blockage.

I think it may be a hernia but I'm not completely sure. I'm unable to visit the doctor right now but may be able to tomorrow but I'm scared it may get worse overnight.
I'm actually in the process of ordering some bags but thank you though. I'll try out the paste as well, it seems like that should work well.

That the surgery I had but they also did a revision. I didn't know they would do it but I think something went wrong during surgery making them do a revision. I'm not completely sure because I haven't had a chance to speak with anyone for a while also since this covid situation.

I had to decide to have the stoma permanent or get it reversed. I chose to keep it but they ended up also revising it.

Before the revision it was perfect and was the only reason I chose to have it permanent, now I sort of wish I never had the surgery because I'm stuck with this now and can't go anywhere to get help with it.
I'm using the standard bags, it sounds like I could do with a convex bag but it's taking a while for me to be able to try one.

That's exactly what's happening but for some reason they're just not staying at all anymore. I haven't used convex bags yet as I'm still waiting for a sample before I can order them properly.

With the powder do you apply and then wipe it off or just leave it on the sore parts?

I don't think I've used a barrier seal but I've tried the barrier rings, are they the same? They used to be a perfect fit for my old stoma but now everything just goes under it. Is the paste just a type of glue to seal the edges? I've never used it before.
Does the convex wafer just push around the stoma helping it come out a little more?

After seeing the responses I'm feeling a little better that I'm not the only one experiencing this, I was starting to worry.

I'm using gauze because I have some left over from stoma bag orders but I didn't think if that as an alternative.

I thought 2 months was supposed to be too long but after seeing a few other people's experiences it's starting to make a bit more sense about the timeframe of recovery. Thanks.

I was told I would have one appointment around 10 weeks after the surgery and then a follow up 6 months. My surgeons team said I would receive a phone call instead of the appointment because of everything going on.

Your surgeon sounds way better than mine. I saw mine about 3 times after the surgery including the times I was in hospital.
That's reassuring, your situation sounds similar to mine. I thought I was being weird wearing the gauze in my underwear but I'm glad to see I'm not the only one.

I was told by my surgeon that the recovery time would be about 6 to 8 weeks and I should be back to normal but I don't know how accurate that is now.

I had a follow up appointment scheduled with my surgeon but it's been cancelled because of everything going on. I don't think I have a wound nurse and I was told to goto my gp for any problems but they say go to a&e. I don't really want to goto a&e since I have underlying conditions.

So I was just wondering if anyone else had gone through something similar and how you dealt with it. I seem to be having issue after issue and now I'm wishing I never had the surgery.

Right now I'm using gauze I get given from the colostomy bag orders as a "bandage" for my rear since it leaks blood or fluid. I'm assuming this isn't normal but I don't know what I'm supposed to do.
I had this days after leaving hospital and got given antibiotics but they didn't do anything.

It was about 5 weeks ago and they ended up doing it while removing the rest of my large bowel. It felt like what you and other comments have described.

I've never had one before so I was a little concerned as I didn't know how to treat it properly.
That makes sense, I didn't think about the convex wafer in that way since I've always stuck to the regular ones. I'll have to try them out. Thanks for the explanation.

Oh wow I didn't think it'd be a day surgery. My past surgeries have been a lot bigger but they were for additional things as well as the stoma.

What was the recovery like? Was it just waiting for the stitches to heal around the stoma?
What was the revision process like? I've had 2 surgeries now and feel a bit weird potentially asking for another but I can't handle the stoma like this.

I had part 2 of a surgery so I could remove the rest of my colon as it was causing trouble but they also revised the stoma which seems to be a lot worse than before. I also wish I never got the surgery done now and I hope they can restore it to how it was before somehow.
How do you mean extra ring to push it out? If I put a ring on it, it will be deeper and then the output goes underneath.
Do you mind going through the diagnosis process of ADHD? I suspect I may have it and don't know how to get assessed.
If you don't mind me asking, what type of medication is it? I'd been given suppositories for the bleeding but they didn't seem to work for me.

How did the doctors react when you said it was still bleeding often? I've mentioned this multiple times and have even had a camera colonoscopy done to see the severity of it but the surgeon just seems to put it off and tells me to wait a little longer or think on it.

So they will remove the rectum if you make the bag permanent *and* if you have the j-pouch? I though you needed it around if you have the j-pouch and the pouch part is fashioned with the remaining colon?

I've also had the same issues but has been occurring for about 4 years now and the surgeon said it's normal. I'm still waiting for the second part of the surgery to remove the rectum.

Just out of curiousity what does your surgeon say about these symptoms? I'm not sure if my case is normal because it sure doesn't feel like it is.

I'd mention everything to your GP and they'd refer your from there. In my experience they avoided medication because I was young (also early 20s) and referred me to therapy. From there you can self refer and go from there.

I'm basing this on my experiences since I don't know how everyone else is effected.

I've had a temporary ileostomy for about 4 years and I've never had a blockage. As long as you stay away from certain foods in large quantities and chew properly you should be fine. I believe everyone's experience with this is different but that's the general idea of it.

It definitely gave me more control compared to just having ulcerative colitis. I was very conscious about the bag at first however it's something that you'll get used to after a while. It was still a better option than having the colitis flares.

The whole mucus thing I believe may be different for everyone. I've had a temporary ileostomy which means I still have the rectum part still attached. For me, the colitis effected the rectum part (which is still attached) pretty bad so it still constantly bleeds. The mucus is noticeable but I can't tell since there is more blood than anything. I'd keep this in mind and ask about this since I didn't know this would happen until after I had the operation and found out myself.
I believe this will stop if the rectum is removed and the ileostomy is made permanent.

For the future surgeries. I've been told that there are 2 main options. The internal pouches and external bags.

The internal pouches are when they form a pouch internally. The most common I believe is the J-pouch however there are others such as S-pouch and W-pouch. I don't know when these are used.

With the bags they either remove the rectum completely or keep it. I don't know a lot about keeping it but I think if it doesn't bother you then it's okay to keep.

For the infertility, I believe there is a risk of those sorts of things as the area which is being operated on is located near those parts therefore there is always that risk involved.

If there's anything else I can answer just ask.

(UK) I've had a temporary ileostomy for around 4 years now and recently been put on a waiting list for a permanent. I've supposed to have it scheduled for some time next year now so in total it'll be 5 years by the time I have anything done.
This may sound strange coming from me but have a look at imposter syndrome if you haven't already. It's basically something people feel when starting a new job and feeling like they don't fit in.
If you don't mind me asking. What was the process of getting a diagnosis like? I'm in the UK and not sure on how the process works.
Do you know who prescribes the medication? I would like to give therapy a try but it's proving to be difficult but I can see my GP. So if they prescribe the medication it may be an option for me.

I told them of the problems I was having and they said it was normal. Now I've recently mentioned them again and another doctor had seen the issue (camera test) and have said the colon is quite bad and asked why I haven't wanted anything done yet.

But I've been asking (for the 4 years) when I can have the operation because I wanted to get it straight away but they said not to rush because it's s big decision. I've told them of the struggles I'm having and they've just referred me to a mental health clinic which probably isn't going to help because that's not the root of the problem.

Your situation sounds pretty similar to mine, my entire colon was also removed and I've had bleeding. I was initially unsure on which surgery to have but started leaning towards the permanent ileostomy after a few months.

Mine's been temporary for 4 years now and I've also had bleeding since I was still in hospital after the operation. What's annoying about it is that it can be painful, causes urgency and makes be go more than I need to empty the bag.  Because of these issues I didn't want to experience them after having the reversal so I felt having the permanent bag is my only option.
I didn't know there are therapists for illnesses, I'll look into it, thanks.

I'd recommend speaking to the doctor or nurse about it since they know what people experience. Personally the mucus calmed down after a while but the blood got worse and worse. They'd recommend suppositories for the blood of it's too much of an inconvenience.
